research.searched: A focused search on 2026-10-16 for when Arion charges its debit card’s yearly fee, and what a close owes: Arion’s own documents, the law that binds it, its incorporation, and the regulator’s guidance. Every source below was read that day; every quote was checked against the file as fetched (saved in the scratchpad’s arion/research, not in the repository).

sources.source: Arion banki, Gjaldskrá greiðslureikninga, Veltureikningur (the payment-account fee sheet), “Dagsetning gjaldskrár/verðskrár: 07.05.2026”
sources.confirms: “Árgjald debetkorts: Árgjald viðskiptavina 24 ára og eldri 950 kr.; Árgjald viðskiptavina 23 ára og yngri 0 kr.”; debit purchases 19 kr from 24, 0 kr under; reissue 1,290 kr.
sources.doesNotConfirm: When in the year the fee is charged, ahead or behind, or anything of a close.

sources.source: Arion banki, Verðskrá einstaklinga (the price list for individuals), “Gildir frá 07.05.2026”, items 13.1 and 13.1.1
sources.confirms: “13.1 Árgjald debetkorts 950 kr.”; “13.1.1 Árgjald debetkorts 23 ára og yngri 0 kr.”

sources.source: Arion banki, Almennir viðskiptaskilmálar (general terms) 18.7.1.15, “Gildistaka: 15. apríl 2026” (in force 15 June 2026, 15 April for a customer who confirms them)
sources.confirms: Ch. 1.1: the terms within Act 114/2021’s scope, “þ.m.t. ákvæði um … greiðslureikninga og greiðslukort”, are a framework contract for payment services in the Act’s sense, of indefinite term. Ch. 5: “Reikningseigandi greiðir kostnað vegna útgáfu og notkunar korts í samræmi við verðskrá bankans … Gjöld vegna korta, svo sem árgjald korta og gjald fyrir útgáfu og endurnýjun, er samkvæmt verðskrá bankans og er skuldfært af reikningi reikningseiganda.” Ch. 4.2 repeats the Act’s first sentence of art. 57(4) (“Ef samið hefur verið um reglubundnar greiðslur skal hlutfallslega tekið tillit til gildistíma uppsagnar við innheimtu greiðslna eftir uppsögn samnings”). Ch. 4.7: fees owed may be debited before an account closes, and “Ef neikvæð staða er á reikningi viðskiptavinar við lokun, t.d. vegna kostnaðarfærslna, getur bankinn jafnframt leitað fullnustu kröfunnar með innheimtu.” Ch. 5.6(k): the bank may close a card whose “árgjald korts hefur ekki verið greitt”. Ch. 11: with these terms “falla úr gildi almennir skilmálar innlánsreikninga, debetkortaskilmálar, kreditkortaskilmálar …”: there are no separate debit-card or deposit-account terms in force to read.
sources.doesNotConfirm: When in the year the card fee is charged, or whether it pays for the year ahead; the terms don’t repeat art. 57(4)’s second sentence (a fee paid ahead refunded).

sources.source: Arion banki, debit-card pages, Icelandic (“Almenn gjöld: Árgjald 950 kr. Færslugjald 19 kr. Viðskiptavinir okkar sem eru 23 ára og yngri greiða hvorki árgjald né færslugjöld af debetkortum.”) and English (“Annual fee 950 kr. … Our customers who are 23 years old and younger pay neither annual fees nor transaction fees”)
sources.confirms: The amount and the age again.
sources.doesNotConfirm: The timing. No card FAQ was found: the terms page (https://www.arionbanki.is/bankinn/regluverk/reglur-og-skilmalar) and its summary are drawn by script, and their HTML lists no document.

sources.source: The official glossary of payment-account terms (Lokaskrá – hugtakalisti), the annex to no. 485/2023, 17 May 2023, Stjórnartíðindi B, published 22 May 2023, as Arion hosts it
sources.confirms: “Árgjald debetkorts: Gjald sem viðskiptavinur greiðir reikningsveitanda einu sinni á ári fyrir debetkort.” A fee paid once a year.
sources.doesNotConfirm: When in the year, or for which year.

sources.source: Lög um greiðsluþjónustu nr. 114/2021 (Iceland’s Act on Payment Services), as published in Stjórnartíðindi A, signed 25 June 2021, published 15 July 2021 (the Official Journal’s text as enacted)
sources.confirms: Art. 57(4): “Ef samið hefur verið um reglubundnar greiðslur á samningstímanum fyrir greiðsluþjónustu samkvæmt rammasamningi skal hlutfallslega tekið tillit til gildistíma uppsagnar við innheimtu greiðslna eftir uppsögn samnings. Ef gjöld vegna greiðsluþjónustu samkvæmt rammasamningi eru greidd fyrir fram skulu þau endurgreidd notanda hlutfallslega, með tilliti til gildistíma uppsagnar.” Art. 57(1): the user may terminate at any time, any agreed notice no longer than a month; 57(2): termination free of charge to the user; 57(3): the provider’s notice at least two months. Art. 41(2): chapter IV (arts. 41 to 60) may be derogated from by contract only where the user isn’t a consumer. Art. 113: the Act implements Directive (EU) 2015/2366 “eins og hún var tekin upp í samninginn um Evrópska efnahagssvæðið með ákvörðun sameiginlegu EES-nefndarinnar nr. 165/2019 frá 14. júní 2019”. Art. 115: in force 1 November 2021, repealing Act 120/2011.
sources.doesNotConfirm: When a card fee is charged; it names no card fee, so that a debit card’s yearly fee is a “gjald vegna greiðsluþjónustu samkvæmt rammasamningi” is SLATE’s reading, supported by Arion’s terms 1.1 putting its cards in the framework contract. It doesn’t say how the share is counted (days or months).

sources.source: The Official Journal’s search, A-deild, “greiðsluþjónustu”, 2022 to 2026; the amending acts it found read: 5/2023 (Lög um greiðslureikninga, art. 30), 62/2024 (art. 48), 27/2025 (art. 10), 78/2025
sources.confirms: None of them amends art. 57: they amend arts. 14 and 97 (5/2023), 5 (62/2024), 82 (27/2025) and 2, 4, 18, 99 and others (78/2025). Act 5/2023 art. 10(3) refers a payment account’s closing fee to art. 57.
sources.doesNotConfirm: That no amendment exists: the search shows its first page only, and the consolidated text (althingi.is/lagas/nuna/2021114.html) couldn’t be read.

sources.confirms: Incorporated into the EEA Agreement by Joint Committee Decision 165/2019, Annex IX, “In force in the EEA: Yes”; the Directive in Icelandic in the EEA Supplement No 87, 17.12.2020, pp. 180 to 272.
sources.doesNotConfirm: Anything about Arion; it isn’t taken as Iceland’s law: the Act is.

sources.source: Directive (EU) 2015/2366, art. 55, as legislation.gov.uk (The National Archives) publishes the Directive
sources.confirms: Art. 55(4): “Charges for payment services levied on a regular basis shall be payable by the payment service user only proportionally up to the termination of the contract. If such charges are paid in advance, they shall be reimbursed proportionally.” Art. 55(6) allows more favourable national rules, which Iceland’s free termination (57(2)) is.
sources.doesNotConfirm: Anything about Arion, or a card fee’s timing.

sources.source: Seðlabanki Íslands (the Central Bank), Spurt og svarað – greiðsluþjónustuveitendur, 2. útgáfa, March 2025
sources.confirms: Nothing on the point: its three pages address providers, not a close’s charges.

notRead: althingi.is (the consolidated Act and its bill): HTTP 403, a Cloudflare challenge, on every request on 2026-10-16, as in brief 09: https://www.althingi.is/lagas/nuna/2021114.html, https://www.althingi.is/lagasafn/pdf/157c/2021114.pdf.

web.archive.org’s copies of the consolidated Act (153c, archived 28 October 2023) and of the Act in Stjórnartíðindi (archived 5 October 2024): found by archive.org’s availability service, but the copies themselves blocked by this container’s egress policy.

The Central Bank’s English translation of Act 114/2021 (https://english.sedlabanki.is/library/Skraarsafn---EN/Laws/Act%20No.%20114%202021%20on%20Payment%20Services.pdf): it now redirects to a 404; cb.is’s law pages are drawn by script, with no document in their HTML.
EUR-Lex (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32015L2366): HTTP 202 with a challenge and no text; the Directive was read from legislation.gov.uk instead.
Arion’s debit-card terms and deposit-account terms as separate documents: none in force (general terms ch. 11), and no earlier copy found.
The Consumer Agency’s (Neytendastofa’s) guidance: a search found none on card fees or a close.
confirmed: The amount and the age: 950 kr a year from 24, 0 kr at 23 and under (the fee sheet and price list, from 7 May 2026; the debit-card pages).
A fee paid once a year (the official glossary, no. 485/2023).
Who pays and from where: the account holder, debited from the account (the general terms, ch. 5).
That Arion’s card terms are a framework contract in the Act’s sense (the general terms, 1.1), and that no separate debit-card terms are in force (ch. 11).

What a close owes whatever the timing, for a consumer: a fee paid ahead comes back in proportion, and a regular one collected after is owed only in proportion to the termination’s effective date (Act 114/2021 art. 57(4), from the Official Journal’s text as enacted; arts. 41, 113, 115).
That the Act carries Directive (EU) 2015/2366 into Icelandic law as incorporated by EEA Joint Committee Decision 165/2019 (the Act’s art. 113; EEA-Lex).
notConfirmed: Whether the 950 kr pays for the card year ahead or the year past.
The day in the year it’s charged (the card’s issue, its renewal, the account’s opening, a fixed date).
How Arion counts a share on a close (days or months), and at whose clock.
Whether art. 57 has been amended since 2021 (the consolidated text couldn’t be read; the amending acts found don’t touch it).
That a debit card’s yearly fee is a fee “vegna greiðsluþjónustu samkvæmt rammasamningi” in art. 57(4)’s sense: SLATE’s reading, as above.

rule.fromASource: What a close owes, whatever the timing: Act 114/2021 art. 57(4), a fee paid ahead refunded in proportion, a regular one collected after only in proportion to the close (with SLATE’s reading that the card’s yearly fee is such a fee).
rule.simulationAssumption: The timing, which no source settles: ARION_CARD_YEAR in src/engine/content/banks-thirteen.ts, labelled in its comment “SLATE SIMULATION ASSUMPTION, UNVERIFIED”, kept apart from the confirmed amount and age (Bank.card.yearly and freeUnder, from the price list). Default: paid ahead, the first on the account’s first night in the life, renewed on the same date a year on by Reykjavík’s calendar (the month’s last day where the date doesn’t exist); on a close the fee paid × the days of that card year left after the closing day ÷ the year’s days (365 or 366) comes back, rounded half up once to the whole króna, against Bank Fees. That the share is counted in days is SLATE’s design choice too.
whyThisDefault: It changes least of what every played life already did: a kept Arion account was charged on its first night, and the opening float counts the same three years (feesToGraduation, unchanged under it).
It is the form Berliner Sparkasse’s price list states for its card (footnote 45, § 675h(3) BGB), so one model serves both banks, and that model was already built and tested.
Under art. 57(4) the holder pays for the same days held either way: the assumption moves when the krónur leave and whether a close gives back or charges, not what a year costs.
rule.configurable: ARION_CARD_YEAR.paid is one word: 'behind' (each charge pays for the card year it ends; a close charges the days used) is implemented and tested beside the default. Each card year is settled by the rule it was opened under (Account.cardYearRule), so changing the setting never charges or refunds a year twice (tested). When a source settles the timing, set paid to it and delete simulated, and the label leaves the screen and the guide.
rule.labelled: On the account’s panel (cardYearWords), under Close It and Cancel It (closingFeesWords), in Other Charges for a primary Arion account, and in the guide’s A Bank At Home: “Its timing is SLATE’s simulation, unverified: Arion’s price list and terms don’t say when in the year it’s charged.” The amount and age are said first, as the price list’s.
rule.edges: A close between Reykjavík’s midnight and New Haven’s on the year’s date, when SLATE’s night opens the next year, finds the last year used up and the next not begun: nothing back, nothing charged (tested). An account that can’t cover the fee is charged it all the same and goes below zero by what’s short, as every SLATE fee takes it, under Arion’s overdraft rule (15.75%, 60 days to the bank’s close), consistent with Arion’s terms 4.7 and 5.6(k); said on the panel.
